title: Fix test for Windows line endings

timeline.message: Fix test for Windows line endings
timeline.author: William Brafford

timeline.body:
Adjustments to the MockTerminal class in #86198 and elsewhere have broken tests that depended on specific line endings. In many cases, this was not what the test was actually trying to check for. This fix makes the strings as system-agnostic as possible, in several cases using the `String#lines` method to handle line endings in a system-agnostic way.

Closes #86294. Closes #86341
We could probably just remove the line ending altogether and use startsWith? This test is trying to assert errors are printed when --silent is used, not check anything about terminal output.

timeline.body: I pushed some more fixes to this branch since the problem is causing a lot of build failures.

timeline.body: No need to parse it using `lines()`, just use `containsString`?

reply.body: My thinking here was that `lines()` gives us a list containing a string which must be exactly `keystore.seed`, which is a stronger check than whether whether the output contains a substring.

timeline.body: Can we not depend on the line separator here?
This seems like a place where we do actually care about the newline. Using `lines()` would mask if we were not printing any newline at all. Could we still assert the length?
Looks good, I have a few suggestions.
